    10	/-!
    11	# The presentation locus for the rank-one Abel map
    12	
    13	`PicRankOneOpen` is the functorial locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer whose pullback to
    14	every affine test admits a tied `PicRankOneLocalPresentation`.  Quantifying after every affine
    15	pullback makes the condition intrinsic on arbitrary test schemes; stability under further
    16	pullback is exactly `picEtMap_comp`.
    17	
    18	The remaining declarations form the corresponding preimages in the widened divisor functor and
    19	in its canonical representing Yoneda functor, together with the restricted Abel transformations.
    20	These are logical subfunctors only.  In particular, this file does not assert that
    21	`PicRankOneOpen` is represented by an open subscheme.  The relative-openness acceptance gate and
    22	the conditional universal-divisor carrier contract are exposed separately in `DivRankOneOpen.lean`.
    23	-/
    24	
    25	set_option autoImplicit false
    26	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    27	
    28	universe u
    29	
    30	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    31	
    32	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    33	
    34	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    35	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    36	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    37	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    38	
    39	noncomputable section
    40	
    41	/-- The rank-one presentation locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer.
    42	
    43	Membership means that every affine pullback of the input plus class admits a local presentation
    44	tied to that pullback.  This is the correct logical subfunctor underlying the future open Picard
    45	locus; no openness or representability assertion is part of this definition. -/
    46	def PicRankOneOpen :
    47	    Subfunctor (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) where
    48	  obj T := {lam | ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    49	      (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    50	    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    51	      ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))}
    52	  map {T T'} f lam hlam A _ _ t := by
    53	    let F := picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)
    54	    have e : F.map t.op (F.map f lam) = F.map (t ≫ f.unop).op lam := by
    55	      apply Subtype.ext
    56	      exact (picEtMap_comp C f.unop t lam.1).symm
    57	    rw [e]
    58	    exact hlam A (t ≫ f.unop)
    59	
    60	/-! ## The public membership contract -/
    61	
    62	/-- The exact producer predicate for the rank-one locus.
    63	
    64	This is intentionally lambda-tied and quantifies over every affine pullback.  In particular, it
    65	is stronger than a field-fibre `h⁰ = 1`/`H¹ = 0` statement: a producer must supply the complete
    66	`PicRankOneLocalPresentation` structure for the pulled-back class. -/
    67	def PicRankOneOpen.LocalPresentationCondition
    68	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    69	    (lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) : Prop :=
    70	  ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    71	    (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    72	    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    73	      ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))
    74	
    75	/-- Unfolded membership in `PicRankOneOpen`, with the presentation tied to the pulled-back
    76	Picard class.  Keeping this predicate named is important for producers in later lanes: a
    77	field-level divisor or chart witness is not a substitute for this arbitrary-affine-pullback
    78	contract. -/
    79	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_iff {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    80	    (lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) :
    81	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T ↔
    82	      ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    83	        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    84	        Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    85	          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam)) := by
    86	  rfl
    87	
    88	/-- Constructor for the exact lambda-tied arbitrary-affine-pullback presentation contract. -/
    89	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentations
    90	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    91	    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
    92	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    93	        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    94	        Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    95	          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))) :
    96	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T :=
    97	  (mem_picRankOneOpen_iff pi lam).mpr h
    98	
    99	/-- Constructor using the named arbitrary-affine producer predicate. -/
   100	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentationCondition
   101	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   102	    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
   103	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.LocalPresentationCondition pi lam) :
   104	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T := by
   105	  exact mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentations pi h
   106	
   107	/-- The inclusion of the public rank-one locus into its degree-genus ambient functor. -/
   108	def picRankOneOpenIncl :
   109	    (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor ⟶ picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ) :=
   110	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).ι
   111	
   112	/-- The same inclusion after the slice-to-big-site `Σ` extension.
   113	
   114	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is a property of presheaves on schemes.  The rank-one functor is
   115	defined on the slice over `Spec k`, so the `Σ` extension is the category-correct carrier for the
   116	relative-open gate below. -/
   117	def picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl :
   118	    Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor ⟶
   119	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) :=
   120	  Over.sigmaExtensionNat (PicRankOneOpen pi).ι
   121	
   122	/-- Relative openness of the public locus, in Mathlib's presheaf sense.
   123	
   124	This is a named acceptance gate rather than an unproved global assertion.  A future geometric
   125	producer discharges it by supplying the represented open pullbacks; no arbitrary `Subfunctor` is
   126	silently treated as an open subscheme. -/
   127	def PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen : Prop :=
   128	  IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi)
   129	
   130	/-! ## The explicit fibre producer contract -/
   131	
   132	/-- A fibre of the rank-one locus over one test class, presented by an open of that test.
   133	
   134	The `exists_factor` field is tied to the displayed class `g` and to an arbitrary source value `v`.
   135	It is the family-level content needed for relative representability; the open immersion itself
   136	supplies uniqueness of the factor.  Thus this structure cannot be inhabited by an unrelated open
   137	or by a fieldwise dimension statement. -/
   138	structure PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented
   139	    {X : Scheme.{u}}
   140	    (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
   141	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ))) where
   142	  W : X.Opens
   143	  fst : yoneda.obj (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶
   144	    Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor
   145	  sq : fst ≫ picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi = yoneda.map W.ι ≫ g
   146	  exists_factor : ∀ (S : Scheme.{u})
   147	    (v : (Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor).obj (Opposite.op S))
   148	    (w : S ⟶ X),
   149	    (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi).app (Opposite.op S) v =
   150	      g.app (Opposite.op S) w →
   151	    ∃ u : S ⟶ (W : Scheme.{u}),
   152	      fst.app (Opposite.op S) u = v ∧ u ≫ W.ι = w
   153	
   154	namespace PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented
   155	
   156	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
   157	variable {g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
   158	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ))}
   159	
   160	/-- The fibre square supplied by `FibrePresented` is a pullback of presheaves. -/
   161	theorem isPullback (D : PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented pi g) :
   162	    IsPullback D.fst (yoneda.map D.W.ι) (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi) g := by
   163	  refine IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app fun S => ?_
   164	  rw [Types.isPullback_iff]
   165	  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
   166	  · exact congrArg (fun φ : yoneda.obj (D.W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶
   167	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) =>
   168	      φ.app S) D.sq
   169	  · rintro u₁ u₂ ⟨-, h₂⟩
   170	    exact (cancel_mono D.W.ι).mp h₂
   171	  · intro v w hvw
   172	    obtain ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩ := D.exists_factor S.unop v w hvw
   173	    exact ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩
   174	
   175	end PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented
   176	
   177	/-- An arbitrary-test fibre producer discharges the relative openness gate. -/
   178	theorem picRankOneOpen_isOpen_of_fibrePresented
   179	    (D : ∀ (X : Scheme.{u})
   180	      (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
   181	        Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ))),
   182	      PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented pi g) :
   183	    PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi := by
   184	  refine MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists ?_
   185	  intro X g
   186	  let d := D X g
   187	  exact ⟨d.W, d.fst, d.W.ι, d.isPullback, inferInstance⟩
   188	
   189	/-- Expose a supplied relative-open certificate without hiding it behind typeclass search. -/
   190	theorem picRankOneOpen_isOpen_of_certificate
   191	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi) : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi :=
   192	  h
   193	
   194	/-- Extract the open immersion supplied by the relative-openness certificate on an arbitrary
   195	pullback.  This is the exact shape consumed by an eventual chart/fibre producer. -/
   196	theorem picRankOneOpen_openPullback
   197	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi)
   198	    {X Z : Scheme.{u}}
   199	    (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
   200	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)))
   201	    (fst : yoneda.obj Z ⟶
   202	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor)
   203	    (snd : Z ⟶ X)
   204	    (hpb : IsPullback fst (yoneda.map snd) (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi) g) :
   205	    IsOpenImmersion snd :=
   206	  h.property g fst snd hpb
   207	
   208	/-- Pullback stability of the public rank-one locus, exposed independently of its definition. -/
   209	theorem picRankOneOpen_map_mem {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   210	    (f : T ⟶ T') {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
   211	    (h : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T) :
   212	    (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map f lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T' :=
   213	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).map f h
   214	
   215	/-- Pullback stability of the public locus, with the base-change direction made explicit. -/
   216	theorem picRankOneOpen_baseChange_mem {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   217	    (f : T ⟶ T') {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
   218	    (h : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T) :
   219	    (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map f lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T' :=
   220	  picRankOneOpen_map_mem pi f h
   221	
   222	/-- The inverse image of `PicRankOneOpen` under the affine widened Abel transformation.
   223	
   224	This name deliberately records only a presentation-theoretic preimage.  It is not the future
   225	open subscheme `DivRankOneOpen`. -/
   226	def divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff :
   227	    Subfunctor (divFunctorAff C (genus C)) :=
   228	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).preimage (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C))
   229	
   230	/-- The same presentation preimage on the Yoneda functor of the canonical genus divisor
   231	representer. -/
   232	def divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter :
   233	    Subfunctor (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)) :=
   234	  (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).preimage
   235	    (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom
   236	
   237	/-- The affine Abel transformation restricted to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
   238	def rankOneAbelAff :
   239	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).toFunctor ⟶
   240	      (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor :=
   241	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).fromPreimage (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C))
   242	
   243	/-- Restrict the canonical representation isomorphism to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
   244	def rankOneRepresenterRestriction :
   245	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor ⟶
   246	      (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).toFunctor :=
   247	  (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).fromPreimage
   248	    (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom
   249	
   250	/-- The represented genus Abel map restricted to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
   251	def rankOneAbelRepresented :
   252	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor ⟶
   253	      (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor :=
   254	  rankOneRepresenterRestriction pi ≫ rankOneAbelAff pi
   255	
   256	/-- Immediate consumer theorem: the restricted represented Abel map lands in the public locus.
   257	The stronger canonical inverse still needs the family-level divisor/evaluation producer; this
   258	theorem records the exact target API that consumer lanes can use today. -/
   259	theorem rankOneAbelRepresented_mem {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   260	    (x : (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).obj T) :
   261	    ((rankOneAbelRepresented pi).app T x :
   262	      (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T :=
   263	  ((rankOneAbelRepresented pi).app T x).property
   264	
   265	end
   266	
   267	end AlgebraicGeometry

    42	degree-`n` divisor families as a presheaf of types on the slice over `Spec k`,

    75

     9	/-!
    10	# The chart-typed divisor functor maps into the WIDENED one (R2)
    11	
    12	`divFamZarToAffVehicle` (`…AffVehicle.lean`) carries a chart-typed vehicle section to a widened
    13	one at each affine open of a test.  Now that both sides are functors —`divFunctor`
    14	(`DivisorFamilyZarFunctor.lean`) and `divFunctorAff` (`…AffMap.lean`) — the comparison can be
    15	stated where a consumer actually uses it: as a **natural transformation** of presheaves on the
    16	slice over `Spec k`.
    17	
    18	## Why this is the shape that matters
    19	
    20	A consumer holding a chart-typed section over a general test `T` does not want to know that the
    21	two carriers agree affine-open by affine-open; it wants to substitute the widened functor for the
    22	chart-typed one and keep its restriction maps.  That is exactly naturality, and it is the
    23	statement `DivRepGlobalData`-style clauses (which are equations between *restrictions*) can
    24	consume.
    25	
    26	The proof is one application of the widened uniqueness `divFamZarAff.mapVal_eq_of`: the
    27	componentwise image of the chart-typed glued value already has the widened pullback property,
    28	because `DivFamZar.toAff_mapAlgHom` turns each clause of the chart-typed `mapVal_spec` into the
    29	corresponding widened clause.  No gluing is redone.
    30	
    31	## The direction, and it is not an omission
    32	
    33	Old → new only.  A widened certificate cover is an arbitrary family of affine opens, and by
    34	`informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 3 §2 / ADDENDUM 4 §4.3 there is a straddling divisor at every
    35	genus `≥ 2` that no fixed pair of `P¹` charts can confine — so no natural transformation back can
    36	exist.  That failure is the content of R2 (protection I-0492), not a gap in this file.
    37	
    38	## Main declarations
    39	
    40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFamZarToAffVehicle_map` — the comparison commutes with restriction along
    41	  an arbitrary morphism of test objects.
    42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFunctorToAff` — the natural transformation `divFunctor ⟶ divFunctorAff`.
    43	-/

    46	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

    65

    67	that the left-hand one has the widened pullback property, and each of its clauses is the
    68	`toAff`-image of a clause of the chart-typed `divFamZar.mapVal_spec`
    69	(`DivFamZar.toAff_mapAlgHom`). -/
    70	theorem divFamZarToAffVehicle_map {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
    71	    (s : divFamZar C π n T) :
    72	    divFamZarToAffVehicle C n π (divFamZar.map C π n f s)
    73	      = divFamZarAff.map C n f (divFamZarToAffVehicle C n π s) := by
    74	  refine divFamZarAff.ext fun W => ?_
    75	  rw [divFamZarToAffVehicle_val, divFamZarAff.map_val]
    76	  refine (divFamZarAff.mapVal_eq_of C n f (divFamZarToAffVehicle C n π s) ?_).symm
    77	  intro W₀ hW₀ V hV

    80	  -- match on the right-hand side.
    81	  rw [divFamZarToAffVehicle_val, ← DivFamZar.toAff_mapAlgHom, ← DivFamZar.toAff_mapAlgHom,
    82	    divFamZar.map_val]
    83	  exact congrArg DivFamZar.toAff (divFamZar.mapVal_spec C π n f s W W₀ hW₀ V hV)

    94	    ext s
    95	    exact divFamZarToAffVehicle_map g.unop s

    99	    (divFunctorToAff C π n).app T s = divFamZarToAffVehicle C n π s :=

    13	gluing keystone (§8.6), and finally a functor `divFunctorAff` with a natural transformation
    14	`divFunctorToAff` out of the chart-typed one (ADDENDUM 9).  What it did **not** have, at every
    15	one of those milestones, is a **consumer**: measured at HEAD, the widened names appeared in zero
    16	files outside the `Picard/DivisorFamilyAff*.lean` family.

    19	(`DivRepAffinePullback.pullGlobal`, `Picard/DivRepGlobalLift.lean`) on the widened functor and
    20	proves the `pull_comp` law there — the one field of `DivRepGlobalData` that is *about* the
    21	functor rather than about a single test.

    23	## What the restatement costs, and why that is the point
    24	
    25	Nothing but a push-forward.  `pullGlobalAff` is `divFamZarToAffVehicle ∘ pullGlobal`, and its
    26	naturality is the chart-typed `pullGlobal_comp` transported along `divFamZarToAffVehicle_map`.

    30	DD-R stack, not merely well-formed.  A functor nothing consumes and a functor everything can
    31	consume look identical to a sorry census and to a job count.

    37	ADDENDUM 4 §4.3 a straddling divisor at genus `≥ 2` is confined by no fixed pair of `P¹` charts.

    39	chart-typed representability datum pushes forward to a compatible family of widened values.

     9	# DAT-B B-5: from pointwise coverage to the sieve condition
    10	
    11	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity.lean` reduced B-6 to `ChartsCoverLocally`, whose statement
    12	is *sieve-theoretic*: for every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the supremum
    13	of the per-chart image sieves is a Zariski covering sieve.  The dat-b row calls that "B-5
    14	verbatim" and says a producer discharges it "by exhibiting one open neighbourhood and one
    15	index per point of `T`".
    16	
    17	**That last sentence was a claim about a bridge nobody had written.**  What B-5's geometry
    18	produces is pointwise: for each point `t` of the test, an open `W ∋ t`, an index `i`, and a
    19	chart point over `W` whose class restricts to `s`.  What `ChartsCoverLocally` asks for is
    20	membership of a Grothendieck topology.  The two are connected by a *cover construction* —
    21	`Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers` at the family `{W t}` indexed by the points of `T` — and the
    22	connection is what this file supplies.
    23	
    24	## Why the bridge is not bookkeeping the producer can inline
    25	
    26	Three things have to line up, and each is a place a lane would stall:
    27	
    28	* the cover must be indexed by a type in the right universe.  Indexing by the points of `T`
    29	  works (`↥T : Type u` for `T : Scheme.{u}`) and is the *only* index available before any
    30	  geometry is known — a producer that tries to index by a chosen finite subcover needs
    31	  quasi-compactness, which no row assumes;
    32	* `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` asks for `Presieve.ofArrows 𝒰.X 𝒰.f ≤ S.arrows`, i.e. a
    33	  statement about the *presieve generated by the cover maps*, so the per-point witness has to
    34	  be produced after destructing `ofArrows` — which binds the point, not an arbitrary map into
    35	  `T`.  This is where the pointwise data is consumed;
    36	* the per-point index makes the target sieve a *supremum*, and `le_iSup` is what turns "some
    37	  chart works at `t`" into "the supremum contains `W t`".  Nothing forces one index to work
    38	  at every point, which is the chart-parameter heterogeneity the dat-b row records — here it
    39	  costs literally nothing, because `iSup` is what the statement already had.
    40	
    41	## Main declarations
    42	
    43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise` — **the bridge**, stated for an
    44	  arbitrary family of sieves: pointwise opens with a per-point index give the supremum sieve
    45	  covering status.  No presheaf, no chart, no `pic⁰`.
    46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` — `ChartsCoverLocally` from exactly the
    47	  data B-5 produces: per test point, an open neighbourhood, an index, and a chart point over
    48	  that open with the right class.  **This is what a coverage lane owes, and nothing more.**
    49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise` — the composite: pointwise
    50	  coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, i.e.
    51	  B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step.
    52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally` — the **converse**, and the reason this
    53	  is a reduction rather than a restatement: the sieve condition gives back an open cover of
    54	  the test on each of whose members some chart hits `s`.  So the pointwise form is not a
    55	  strengthening chosen to be provable.
    56	-/

    73	/-! ## The bridge, with no chart content
    74	
    75	Stated for an arbitrary family of sieves on an arbitrary scheme, because that is all it uses:
    76	the coverage half of B-5 is a statement about the *site*, and mixing it with the presheaf
    77	statement is what made it look gated. -/
    78	
    79	/-- **Pointwise data gives a covering supremum sieve.**
    80	
    81	If every point `t` of `T` has an open neighbourhood `W t` and an index `idx t` such that the
    82	inclusion `(W t).ι` lies in the `idx t`-th sieve, then the supremum of the family is a
    83	Zariski covering sieve of `T`.
    84	
    85	The proof is the cover `{W t}_{t : ↥T}` — jointly surjective because `t ∈ W t`, open
    86	immersions because they are opens inclusions — fed to `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`, and
    87	then `le_iSup` at the index of the destructed point.
    88	
    89	Note there is **no compatibility condition between different points**: `idx` is an arbitrary
    90	function.  That is why chart-parameter heterogeneity (dat-b row, `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree`)
    91	costs nothing here — a supremum sieve never asks its members to agree. -/
    92	theorem mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {T : Scheme.{u}}
    93	    (Sv : ι → Sieve T) (W : ↥T → T.Opens) (hW : ∀ t, t ∈ W t) (idx : ↥T → ι)
    94	    (hmem : ∀ t, (Sv (idx t)).arrows (W t).ι) :
    95	    (⨆ i, Sv i) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T := by
    96	  refine Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mpr
    97	    ⟨Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers (↥T) (fun t => (W t : Scheme.{u})) (fun t => (W t).ι)
    98	      (fun t => ⟨t, ⟨t, hW t⟩, rfl⟩) (fun t => inferInstance), ?_⟩
    99	  rintro V g ⟨t⟩
   100	  exact le_iSup Sv (idx t) _ (hmem t)

   103	
   104	variable (C) in
   105	/-- **THE B-5 PACKAGING**: `ChartsCoverLocally` from pointwise coverage.
   106	
   107	The hypothesis is exactly the shape the coverage geometry delivers, and is worth reading
   108	field by field against `w4-datb` §1.2.  For every test `T`, every degree-zero class `s` on
   109	it, and every point `t` of `T`:
   110	
   111	* `W` — an open neighbourhood of `t`.  In the intended instantiation this is
   112	  `chartLocusOpens` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`), whose openness is CHART-U(b) and is
   113	  unconditional since `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` was discharged;
   114	* `i` — the chart index, chosen *at `t`*.  Per-point by construction, which is what the
   115	  I-0204 non-uniformity of the twist exponent `m` requires;
   116	* `x` — a point of the `i`-th chart scheme over `W`, i.e. the divisor family the coverage
   117	  argument produces at the splitting field of `κ(t)`;
   118	* `hx` — that its class is `s` restricted to `W`.
   119	
   120	Given that, the sieve condition holds.  So a coverage lane never has to mention `Sigma.desc`,
   121	a coproduct of yoneda presheaves, a covering sieve, or a Grothendieck topology: it produces
   122	four things at a point and this lemma does the rest.
   123	
   124	**What this does not do.**  It does not produce the pointwise data — that is B-5's geometry
   125	and its residue (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation) is recorded on the dat-b row.
   126	It removes the site-theoretic layer between that geometry and B-6, which had never been
   127	written down and which the row described as though it were already there. -/
   128	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   129	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   130	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
   131	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
   132	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
   133	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
   134	  intro T s
   135	  choose W hW i x hx using h T s
   136	  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun t => ⟨x t, hx t⟩
   137	
   138	variable (C) in
   139	/-- **B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step**: pointwise coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance.
   140	
   141	The composite of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` with `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc`.
   142	Recorded because it is the statement a lane closing coverage wants to cite: the *only*
   143	remaining input to the `[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]`
   144	instance that three files carry as an unproduced `variable` is the pointwise data above. -/
   145	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   146	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   147	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
   148	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
   149	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
   150	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
   151	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc f (chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise C f h)

   153	/-! ## The converse: the pointwise form is not a strengthening
   154	
   155	A reduction whose hypothesis is strictly stronger than its conclusion is a weakening in
   156	disguise, and the memory `reduction-needs-its-converse` is about exactly this failure.  Here
   157	the converse holds — modulo the one difference that is genuinely there and is named. -/
   158	
   159	variable (C) in
   160	/-- **`ChartsCoverLocally` gives back an open cover on whose members a chart hits `s`.**
   161	
   162	The converse direction, and the check that the pointwise hypothesis above is the right one.
   163	From the sieve condition one extracts a Zariski cover of `T` by `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`
   164	and reads the supremum membership at each cover map.
   165	
   166	**The one honest difference**, and it is why this is stated with a general `Y ⟶ T` rather than
   167	an open of `T`: `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` returns a cover by *arbitrary* schemes with
   168	open-immersion maps, not by opens of `T`.  Those are the same up to isomorphism
   169	(`Scheme.Hom.isoOpensRange`) but not on the nose, so the converse produces a cover map where
   170	the hypothesis consumed an opens inclusion.  For the purpose this serves — showing the
   171	pointwise data is *available*, hence not a hypothesis chosen for provability — a cover map is
   172	exactly as good, and pretending otherwise would need a transport that adds nothing. -/
   173	theorem pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   174	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   175	    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) (T : Scheme.{u})
   176	    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) :
   177	    ∃ (𝒰 : T.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @IsOpenImmersion)),
   178	      ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ (i : ι) (x : 𝒰.X j ⟶ X i),
   179	        (f i).app (op (𝒰.X j)) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (𝒰.f j).op s := by
   180	  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle⟩ := Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mp (h T s)
   181	  refine ⟨𝒰, fun j => ?_⟩
   182	  have hj := hle (𝒰.X j) (𝒰.f j) (Presieve.ofArrows.mk j)
   183	  rw [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply] at hj
   184	  obtain ⟨S, ⟨i, rfl⟩, x, hx⟩ := hj
   185	  exact ⟨i, x, hx⟩
   186	
   187	end

     8	/-!
     9	# DAT-B B-6: the local-surjectivity half of the `(f, hf)` handoff
    10	
    11	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) needs two things beyond the
    12	charts: the `hf` certificate (C9b, reduced in `Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`) and the
    13	instance
    14	
    15	```
    16	[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]
    17	```
    18	
    19	which is dat-b row B-6.  Three files carry that instance as a `variable`
    20	(`JacobianDataCharts.lean:117`, `JacobianDataAbelSurj.lean:183`,
    21	`JacobianDataAbelImage.lean:131`) and **nothing anywhere produces one**.  This file supplies
    22	the producer, in the form that DAT-B's coverage statement can actually feed.
    23	
    24	## What local surjectivity unfolds to, and why that matters here
    25	
    26	Mathlib's `Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J f` has a single field: for every object `T` and
    27	every section `s` of the target at `T`, the *image sieve* of `s` — the sieve of maps
    28	`g : T' ⟶ T` along which `s` pulls back into the image of `f` — is a covering sieve.
    29	
    30	For the Zariski topology on schemes that is exactly the geometric statement dat-b row B-5
    31	proves: **every degree-zero class on a test is, locally on that test, a chart value**.  So
    32	B-6 is not a further geometric obligation on top of B-5 — it is B-5 phrased against
    33	mathlib's sieve-theoretic interface, plus the bookkeeping that turns a family of charts into
    34	`Sigma.desc`.
    35	
    36	The bookkeeping is what this file provides, and it is not trivial: the section must be hit
    37	by *some* chart of the family, and `Sigma.desc` must be shown to see it.  That is
    38	`ChartsCoverLocally` below.
    39	
    40	## The honest scope, stated up front
    41	
    42	`ChartsCoverLocally` is the hypothesis, not a theorem.  Its content is B-5 and B-5's residue
    43	is recorded on the dat-b roadmap row (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation).  What
    44	this file establishes is that **nothing else** stands between B-5 and the instance the
    45	producer needs — in particular no compatibility across charts, because `Sigma.desc` has
    46	none to check.
    47	
    48	## Main declarations
    49	
    50	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartsCoverLocally` — the coverage hypothesis, stated exactly as the
    51	  image sieve of `Sigma.desc` being covering, but spelled in terms of the individual charts
    52	  so a producer never has to reason about the coproduct.
    53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc` — **B-6**: that hypothesis gives the
    54	  instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
    55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_forall_surjective` — the degenerate sufficient
    56	  condition (a chart that is surjective on points of every test already covers), recorded so
    57	  the hypothesis is visibly *satisfiable* and not a disguised falsehood.
    58	-/
    59	
    60	set_option autoImplicit false
    61	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    62	
    63	universe u
    64	
    65	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    66	
    67	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    68	
    69	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    70	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    71	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    72	
    73	noncomputable section
    74	
    75	variable (C) in
    76	/-- **The coverage hypothesis of DAT-B, stated per chart rather than on the coproduct.**
    77	
    78	For every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the maps into `T` along which `s`
    79	becomes the value of *some* chart of the family form a Zariski covering sieve.
    80	
    81	This is dat-b row B-5 verbatim — "every `pic⁰` point is Zariski-locally a chart point" — with
    82	one deliberate design choice: the sieve is described through the individual `f i`, so a
    83	producer discharges it by exhibiting, for each point of `T`, one open neighbourhood and one
    84	index.  It never has to mention `Sigma.desc` or the coproduct of yoneda presheaves.  Turning
    85	that into the coproduct form is `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc` below. -/
    86	def ChartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    87	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) : Prop :=
    88	  ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)),
    89	    (⨆ i, Presheaf.imageSieve (f i) s) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T
    90	
    91	/-- **B-6**: the coverage hypothesis gives the local-surjectivity instance that
    92	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
    93	
    94	The proof is the bookkeeping the row's name hides: the image sieve of `Sigma.desc f` contains
    95	the image sieve of every individual `f i` — because a `T'`-point of `X i` gives a `T'`-point
    96	of the coproduct through `Sigma.ι` — hence contains their supremum, and a sieve containing a
    97	covering sieve is covering.
    98	
    99	Note what is *not* needed: no compatibility between charts, and no injectivity.  `Sigma.desc`
   100	imposes no coherence condition across indices (the observation `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean`
   101	makes for `hf`, here again for coverage), so a heterogeneous atlas is admissible for B-6 on
   102	exactly the same footing as a homogeneous one. -/
   103	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   104	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   105	    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) :
   106	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) where
   107	  imageSieve_mem {T} s := by
   108	    refine Scheme.zariskiTopology.superset_covering ?_ (h T s)
   109	    refine iSup_le fun i => ?_
   110	    rintro T' g ⟨t, ht⟩
   111	    -- transport the witness along `Sigma.ι` and use `Sigma.ι_desc`
   112	    refine ⟨(Sigma.ι (fun j => yoneda.obj (X j)) i).app (op T') t, ?_⟩
   113	    rw [← ht, ← NatTrans.comp_app_apply, Sigma.ι_desc f i]
   114	
   115	/-- **The hypothesis is satisfiable, checked rather than assumed.**
   116	
   117	If one chart of the family is surjective on the points of every test, the coverage hypothesis
   118	holds — its image sieve is already the maximal sieve.  This is the degenerate case (and not
   119	the geometric situation: no single Abel chart is surjective on all tests), but it rules out
   120	the failure mode where a `Prop`-valued hypothesis turns out to be unsatisfiable and the
   121	"reduction" above is therefore vacuous.
   122	
   123	Compare the two-sided check in `Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`: there the question was whether the
   124	datum was too *weak*; here it is whether it is too *strong*. -/
   125	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_forall_surjective {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   126	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (i : ι)
   127	    (hi : ∀ T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ, Function.Surjective ((f i).app T)) :
   128	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
   129	  intro T s
   130	  refine Scheme.zariskiTopology.superset_covering ?_
   131	    (Scheme.zariskiTopology.top_mem T)
   132	  intro T' g _
   133	  exact le_iSup (fun j => Presheaf.imageSieve (f j) s) i g (hi (op T') _)
   134	
   135	end
   136	
   137	end AlgebraicGeometry
